headline: Council approves Comcast conduit at 75 Riverside Avenue and $200,000 for 448 High Street soil cleanup.
summary: The council approved a Comcast conduit project at 75 Riverside Avenue. It also approved $45,470 for firefighter turnout gear and $200,000 for soil cleanup at 448 High Street. Several other items were referred to committees or departments, and one was tabled.
decisions: Approved resolution honoring the closing of the Congregational Church of West Medford Sanctuary United Church of Christ, 7-0.
Approved a request for a cost report on longer vacation time for city employees, and referred it to the administration and finance committee, 7-0.
Approved a resolution supporting the Tufts University resident assistants in their fight for a fair contract, 7-0.
Asked the Energy and Environment Committee for a draft ordinance on black plastic takeout containers, and referred the paper to the Public Health and Community Safety Committee.
Referred to the administration a request for an update on the vacant Veterans Department director position, 7-0.
Approved the Comcast grant of location to install underground conduit and manholes at 75 Riverside Avenue, with the engineering division's conditions, 7-0.
Approved a license for LSM Limited, doing business as Pavement Coffeehouse, at 177 College Avenue, 7-0.
Referred the linkage fee ordinance update to the Community Development Board, 7-0.
Approved two legal settlements of $5,000 each: Frank Pavaleo versus City of Medford and Vivian Wright versus City of Medford, 7-0.
Approved $45,470 from the capital stabilization fund for firefighter turnout gear and $200,000 for soil remediation at 448 High Street, 7-0.
Approved moving $57,870 from the Roberts Elementary accelerated repair project to the Missitug and Brooks elementary school projects, 7-0.
Referred the city charter update request to the Department of Elections and to the mayor, 7-0.
Referred the proposed sale of two McCormick Avenue city parcels to committee of the whole, as amended, 7-0.
Approved sending a comment letter to the MWRA Cambridge and Somerville combined sewer overflow project team, 6-1.
Tabled the item on capital and general stabilization funding for the police chief search.
Approved cutting the law department supplemental appropriation and asking the mayor for an engagement letter for an outside review, 7-0.
Approved three board and commission appointments, 7-0.
discussion: Union members of the Tufts resident assistants described proposed cuts to housing, meal swipes, and stipends. They said a tentative first-year agreement had been reached while talks on later years continue.

Members discussed the city charter. A legal opinion said the charter took effect by law and that the city council is responsible for recodification, while the council said it still needs certification from the Department of Elections.

Members debated whether to keep funding the law department for another month. They cited unanswered questions about legal costs, an outside review the mayor had agreed to, and the lack of an administration representative at the meeting.

Members and residents discussed a proposal to sell two city-owned parcels on McCormick Avenue for affordable housing. A resident said nearby residents had not been told, and members asked for a review of all city-owned parcels.

Speakers on the sewer overflow letter disagreed. One said the proposed plan is real progress and that water quality matters more than eliminating all overflows. Others urged a stronger plan with no sewage discharges into the rivers.
